\chapter{The Letter That Ends Ram}
\label{ch:mw-letter-ends-ram}
\hlchaptermodality{43}

\begin{chapteropening}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 43: i can write the letter ma, and find it at the end of the first word of this book.

\section[ma]{\mw{म} (ma) — the letter that ends \mw{राम}}

\label{lesson:MW-W43-ma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \mw{अ} and \mw{उ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\mw{राम}} (\emph{rām}), \textquotedblleft{}Ram\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \mw{म}}
\textbf{\mw{म}} — \emph{ma}, the sound \emph{m}.

It ends \textbf{\mw{राम}} (\emph{rām}), the name in the greeting \textbf{\mw{राम}-\mw{राम} \mw{सा}}, the first words in this book. The first chapter built \textbf{\mw{राम}} from \textbf{\mw{र}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}} and \textbf{\mw{म}}, and gave \textbf{\mw{र}} and \textbf{\mw{ा}} lessons of their own. \textbf{\mw{म}} gets its own lesson now.

\subsection*{Writing: \mw{म}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/MW-W43-ma-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \mw{म} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: descend the left stem, circle clockwise through the loop, and sweep right
  \item \textbf{2.} lift, then descend the right stem
  \item \textbf{3.} lift, then draw the shirorekha left-to-right — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 2.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: JackPotte, ‘Devanagari m \mw{म}.gif’, strokes 1–3, Wikimedia Commons, 29 March 2009.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\mw{राम}} and point at \mw{म} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \mw{म} three times, saying \emph{m} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \mw{उ}, then \mw{म}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\mw{राम}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \mw{म}? (\textbf{ma}, \emph{m}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\mw{राम}}, \emph{rām}, \textquotedblleft{}Ram\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
